id_and_class.summary: Jaegwon Kim holds that mental properties supervene on physical ones: there is no mental difference without a physical difference. His causal exclusion argument then forces a choice, since an irreducible mental cause would either overdetermine physical effects or be causally idle. Kim concluded that mental properties must reduce to physical ones to have causal power, while conceding that qualia resist functional reduction.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: No Mental Difference Without a Physical Difference

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Mental properties are fixed by physical properties: anything physically identical is psychologically identical. Supervenience describes this dependence without explaining how the physical produces the mental.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Kim’s view shifted over his career: identity theory, then non-reductive physicalism built on supervenience, then reductive physicalism. Later he accepted a version of property dualism for qualia, which he called something near enough to physicalism.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Supervenient dependence (mental properties are fixed by physical ones; Kim held they must reduce to be causally efficacious)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Kim treats functionally definable mental properties as reducible. Subjective phenomenal properties are the exception he could not reduce.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Kim held that phenomenal properties are not functionally definable and so are functionally irreducible, adding that if functional reduction does not work for qualia, nothing will.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A causally closed physical domain, physical properties that fix mental ones, and, in his later view, phenomenal properties that exceed physical description.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Kim believed any correct account of the mind would come from natural science rather than philosophy or psychology.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Mental states realized by physical states, where one mental state can be realized by different physical systems (multiple realizability).

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Mental causation; phenomenal consciousness (qualia); the mind-body relation generally.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The causal exclusion argument: every physical event with a cause has a sufficient physical cause, so an irreducible mental cause would produce overdetermination. Mental causes must therefore be identical to physical causes or be epiphenomenal.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Mental states are causally efficacious only if they reduce to physical states, as in the identity of pain with C-fiber firing. Irreducible mental properties would be excluded by their physical bases.
core_claims_and_evidence: Things exactly alike in all physical properties cannot differ in mental properties.
Supervenience allows the same psychology to be realized in different physical systems, consistent with functionalism and multiple realizability.
The causal exclusion argument defeats non-reductive physicalism, which wants the mental to be irreducible, dependent, and causally efficacious all at once.
Phenomenal properties are not functionally definable, so physicalism cannot survive intact and in its entirety.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical: metaphysical argument from supervenience and the causal closure of the physical.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Supervenience states a dependency, not a mechanism, so it explains nothing about how brains produce minds. Kim’s own exclusion argument threatens to make qualia epiphenomenal once he grants that they are irreducible.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Kim admitted that physical descriptions of the brain seem unable to account for qualia, leaving a mental residue that physicalism cannot absorb.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Kim pressed physicalism to its limit and found a residue. He still regarded physicalism as the most comprehensive worldview and rejected supernatural explanation as offering one riddle in place of another.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since every mental difference requires a physical difference, no mental life can continue once the physical basis is gone.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Kim held that mind is a natural phenomenon and dismissed supernatural explanation.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Kim's Supervenience (Landscape of Consciousness entry), Jaegwon Kim
